relevance_reason: Case series of 25 individuals from 22 families with heterozygous CACNA1C variants and a mainly neurological phenotype (developmental delay, hypotonia, language delay, skeletal anomalies, epilepsy) without Timothy syndrome or long QT. It also includes patch clamp functional studies. This paper defines the NEDHLSS phenotype.

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) reported 25 individuals from 22 families with heterozygous CACNA1C variants. Their phenotype was mainly neurological and variably included developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism, hypotonia, epilepsy, and ataxia. They did not have significant cardiac manifestations or other features of Timothy syndrome. The authors noted broad phenotypic differences between individuals with truncating and nontruncating variants.
quotes: Here we describe 25 new individuals from 22 families with novel variants in the CACNA1C gene presenting with a predominantly neurological phenotype, variably including developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism, hypotonia, epilepsy, and ataxia, in the absence of significant cardiac manifestations or additional features of Timothy syndrome.
Thirteen individuals are male, and 12 are female. Age at most recent follow-up ranges from 10 months to 40 years (median age 6.8 years).

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) found the CACNA1C variants by exome sequencing or an intellectual disability gene panel, in cases ascertained through GeneMatcher and ClinVar. Thirteen unrelated individuals had missense variants, 1 had an in-frame deletion, and 11 individuals from 8 families had predicted truncating variants. All nontruncating variants and all but 3 truncating variants occurred de novo. None of the variants were present in gnomAD, 1000 Genomes, or the Exome Variant Server. All missense variants were at highly conserved positions and were predicted to be damaging.
quotes: Thirteen unrelated individuals have missense variants in CACNA1C, one individual has an in-frame deletion, and 11 individuals from 8 families have predicted truncating variants, including one canonical splice variant. All the non-truncating variants and all but three of the truncating variants occurred de novo.
None of the variants in our cohort are found in public databases, including the Broad Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD)
All missense variants occur at highly conserved positions and are predicted by in silico models to be damaging (Mutation Taster, Poly-Phen2, SIFT).

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) described 14 individuals with de novo nontruncating CACNA1C variants. All had developmental delay or intellectual disability. Nine were nonverbal and 6 were nonambulatory at last follow-up. One had a formal diagnosis of autism and 6 others had autistic features. Twelve were hypotonic and 4 had ataxia. Prenatal findings included reduced fetal movement (3 of 14), bilateral clubfoot (2 of 14), and oligohydramnios (2 of 14). The course was consistent with a static neurodevelopmental disorder. Brain MRI was normal apart from an incidental arachnoid cyst in 1 individual and prominent cerebellar folia in another.
quotes: All 14 individuals with non-truncating variants have a history of developmental delays or intellectual disability. Two individuals, after early delays, currently have a learning disability. Nine individuals are non-verbal at most recent follow-up, and six are non-ambulatory
Twelve of 14 individuals in this group are hypotonic, and four are described as having abnormal balance and coordination (ataxia).
prenatal history was remarkable for reduced fetal movement (n=3/14), bilateral clubfoot detected on prenatal ultrasound (n=2/14), and oligohydramnios (n=2/14).

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) found epilepsy in 10 of 14 individuals with nontruncating CACNA1C variants. Onset ranged from 2 months to 8 years. Both generalized and focal epilepsies occurred, including West syndrome/infantile spasms, myoclonic seizures, and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Seizures were fever-sensitive in 3 individuals and medically refractory in 4. EEG findings were not consistent across the cohort.
quotes: Ten of 14 individuals in our cohort with non-truncating variants have epilepsy, with onset ranging from 2 months to 8 years.
Both generalized and focal epilepsy disorders were reported. Fever sensitivity was reported in 3 individuals. Epilepsy was medically refractory in 4 individuals.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Febrile seizure (within the age range of 3 months to 6 years)

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) found orthopedic abnormalities in 12 of 14 individuals with nontruncating CACNA1C variants. Two had bilateral clubfoot with congenital finger contractures and 2 others had persistently adducted thumbs. Other findings were kyphosis or scoliosis (2 of 14), congenital hip dysplasia (3 of 14), syndactyly (2 of 14), and joint hypermobility (3 of 14).
quotes: Orthopedic abnormalities were common in individuals with non-truncating variants (n = 12/14). Two of the individuals had bilateral clubfoot and congenital finger contractures. Two additional individuals had persistently adducted thumbs.
Additional orthopedic abnormalities include kyphosis or scoliosis (n=2/14); congenital hip dysplasia (n=3/14); syndactyly (n=2/14); and joint hypermobility (n=3/14).

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) reported ECGs in 11 individuals with nontruncating variants. Nine were normal. One individual (P13, p.Val1411Leu) had prolonged QT with T-wave alternans on Holter monitoring, and another had a possible ventricular conduction delay. Echocardiograms showed only minor findings. No individual had the physical features of Timothy syndrome.
quotes: One individual had mildly prolonged QTc on routine ECG at 7 years of age. Holter monitoring in this individual found significant QT prolongation, especially at higher heart rates (decreased repolarization reserve), and evidence of repolarization instability with macroscopic T wave alternans.
Only one of the individuals in our cohort (P13; p.Val1411Leu) is known to have cardiac disease (prolonged QT), and none has physical features of Timothy syndrome

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) described 11 individuals from 8 families with truncating CACNA1C variants. Most had essentially normal early motor development and walked independently. Ten of 11 had delayed expressive language. Five had autism, 3 of whom were nonverbal. Only 1 had seizures and only 3 had hypotonia. Four had poor balance or coordination and 2 had tremor. Recurrent infections were reported in 4 individuals. All 5 ECGs performed were normal.
quotes: Five of 11 individuals with truncating variants have been diagnosed with autism, and 3 of these individuals are considered non-verbal.
Only 1/11 of these individuals has a history of seizures, and this individual is currently seizure-free without treatment. Only three of the individuals in this group have hypotonia
10/11 individuals in this group had delayed expressive language, whereas early motor development was essentially normal in all but one patient.

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) found that 3 truncating variants were paternally inherited and segregated with neurodevelopmental abnormalities in the families. Penetrance and expressivity appeared variable among family members with truncating variants.
quotes: The three truncating variants that were inherited segregated with neurodevelopmental abnormalities in the families.
Finally, there appeared to be variable penetrance and expressivity of features amongst different family members with truncating variants.

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) observed that individuals with nontruncating variants had more severe global developmental delay or intellectual disability and more motor impairment. Epilepsy was also much more common in this group, affecting more than two-thirds. Individuals with truncating variants had more selective expressive language deficits and autism was more common among them.
quotes: As a group, the individuals with non-truncating variants had more severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability and motor impairment compared to those with truncating variants.
Epilepsy was much more common in the group with non-truncating variants, present in more than two-thirds of individuals.

findings.statement: In a patient (P12) with severe intellectual disability, myoclonic seizures beginning at 6 months, and kyphoscoliosis, Rodan et al. (2021) identified a de novo heterozygous c.4222C>G (p.Leu1408Val) variant in CACNA1C. In patch clamp studies in HEK293 cells, current density was reduced to about 30% of control while protein expression was unchanged, consistent with loss of function.
quotes: Cav1.2 (p.Leu1408Val) displays an overall reduction in current density (Figure 2) with unaltered activation kinetics compared WT Cav1.2.

The Leu1408Val variant appears to have a clear effect on overall channel activity, as current density associated with this variant was significantly reduced to approximately 30% of control, but the protein expression was unchanged.

findings.statement: In a female patient (P9) with moderate to severe intellectual disability and seizures beginning at 6 years, Rodan et al. (2021) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1969C>T (p.Leu657Phe) variant in CACNA1C. In patch clamp studies, the variant significantly increased calcium current, with a hyperpolarizing shift in activation and about 2-fold higher protein levels, consistent with gain of function.
quotes: A more pronounced, statistically significant enhancement of calcium current was observed with the p.Leu657Phe variant (Figure 2).
The gain-of-function effect of the Leu657Phe variant is most likely explained by an increase in protein expression, as both the current density and protein level increased by approximately 2-fold.

findings.statement: In a male patient (P8) with intellectual disability, autism, fever-sensitive generalized epilepsy, and kyphosis, Rodan et al. (2021) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1841T>C (p.Leu614Pro) variant in CACNA1C. Patch clamp studies showed modest current increases with a hyperpolarizing shift in activation, but the increase was not statistically significant. The Results described the variant as gain of function and the Discussion as a neutral effect.
quotes: Modest current increases were observed with the p.Leu614Pro variant, but were not statistically significant (Figure 2).
Missense variants (p.Leu614Pro and p.Leu657Phe) appear to transmit gain-of-function properties to the channel.

findings.statement: In a male patient (P7) with severe developmental delay, myoclonic and generalized tonic-clonic seizures, bilateral clubfoot, and adducted thumbs, Rodan et al. (2021) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1841T>G (p.Leu614Arg) variant in CACNA1C. Patch clamp studies with CACNB2 showed no statistically significant change in current or gating.
quotes: The p.Leu614Arg variant did not appear to confer any statistically significant change in current or properties of voltage-dependent gating (see Figure 2).

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) identified other de novo heterozygous nontruncating CACNA1C variants in their cohort: p.Phe166Leu (c.496T>C), p.Lys177Arg (c.530A>G), p.Arg324Trp (c.970C>T), p.Val403Met (c.1207G>A), p.Leu601Arg (c.1802T>G), p.Met611Thr (c.1832T>C), p.Ile743del (c.2227_2229delATC), and p.Val1187Ala (c.3560T>C). Missense variants clustered in a linker segment of domain II (exon 13) and in domain IV (exon 35).
quotes: p.Phe166Leu | p.Lys177Arg | p.Arg324Trp | p.Val403Met | p.Leu601Arg | p.Met611Thr
there is a clustering of missense variants in one of the linker segments of DII (exon 13) and DIV (exon 35)

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) identified de novo heterozygous variants at codon Val1411 of CACNA1C in 2 unrelated patients. P13, with severe intellectual disability, infantile spasms evolving to Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and prolonged QT, carried c.4231G>C (p.Val1411Leu). P14, an infant with severe global developmental delay, generalized epilepsy beginning at 2 months, hip dysplasia, syndactyly, and adducted thumbs, carried c.4231G>T (p.Val1411Leu).
quotes: Only one of the individuals in our cohort (P13; p.Val1411Leu) is known to have cardiac disease (prolonged QT)

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) identified heterozygous truncating CACNA1C variants in 11 individuals from 8 families. De novo variants were p.Gln80Leufs*49 (c.239_244delAGCGGAinsTTGCAGCTCC), p.Val996Trpfs*19 (c.2926delG), p.Arg1377Profs*61 (c.4129dup), and p.Leu1518Profs*3 (c.4553del). Paternally inherited variants were p.Arg161* (c.481C>T; in 1 of 2 relatives the variant was de novo), p.Trp528* (c.1584G>A), and p.Arg1989* (c.5860C>T). A splice variant, c.2663+1G>C, was not paternal. All truncating variants except p.Arg1989*, which lies in the last exon, were predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay.
quotes: p.Gln80Leufs*49 | p.Arg161* | p.Arg161* | p.Trp528* | splice | p.Val996Trpfs*19 | p.Arg1377Profs*61 | p.Leu1518Profs*3 | p.Arg1989*
c.239_244delAGCGGAinsTTGCAGCTCC | c.481C>T | c.481C>T | c.1584G>A | c.2663+1G>C | c.2926delG | c.4129dup | c.4553del | c.5860C>T
One truncating variant we describe occurs in exon 45/45, potentially escaping nonsense-mediated decay.

findings.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) concluded that both gain and loss of CACNA1C function can cause a neurological phenotype. They noted gnomAD constraint metrics consistent with haploinsufficiency (pLI 1.0). They suggested that the more severe phenotype with loss-of-function missense variants than with whole-gene or exonic deletions favors a dominant-negative effect. They also cautioned that their functional studies used only the canonical transcript and that the choice of accessory subunit may have affected the results.
quotes: The finding that both CACNA1C gain of function and loss of function can result in a neurological phenotype is not unexpected, and there is a precedent for other CNS-expressed calcium channels to be dosage sensitive (eg. CACNA1A).

The more severe neurodevelopmental and epilepsy phenotype in patients with missense, predicted loss-of-function variants compared to those with whole gene/exonic deletions would better support a dominant-negative effect.

relevance_reason: The paper reports CACNA1C variants in patients with a neurodevelopmental phenotype: hypotonia, developmental delay, epilepsy, syndactyly and other skeletal or limb anomalies, and learning disability. This includes a de novo missense variant in an infant with neonatal-onset epileptic encephalopathy.

findings.statement: Bozarth et al. (2018) described a girl (Patient 1) of English/Ukrainian ancestry, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who had neonatal-onset epileptic encephalopathy. Tonic and tonic-myoclonic seizures began within hours of birth and evolved into epileptic tonic spasms at 3 months. The seizures did not respond to multiple antiepileptic drugs, although clobazam reduced them. She had profound axial and appendicular hypotonia, no developmental progress at 18 months, inability to fixate or track visually, and severe sleep-wake disturbance. She also had laryngomalacia, bilateral clubfeet, 3-4 finger and 2-3 toe syndactyly, camptodactyly, micrognathia, downturned corners of the mouth, frontal bossing, scant hair, inverted nipples, mild optic nerve hypoplasia, anal stenosis, and dysphagia requiring a gastrostomy tube. EEG showed distinctive diffuse excessive fast activity, brain MRI was normal, and echocardiogram and Holter monitoring were normal.
quotes: She was found to have profound axial and appendicular hypotonia, laryngomalacia with stridor, bilateral clubbed feet, bilateral 3–4 finger and 2–3 toe syndactyly, and camptodactyly.
Her seizures started within a few hours of birth with numerous subtle tonic seizures as well as prolonged tonic and tonic-myoclonic seizures per day.
Her first EEG at 5 days of life demonstrated very distinctive features with diffuse excessive fast activities admixed with other frequency activities and subtle tonic seizures.

findings.statement: In Patient 1, who had neonatal-onset epileptic encephalopathy, Bozarth et al. (2018) used trio exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the CACNA1C gene: c.4087G>A (NM_000719.6), predicting p.V1363M. The variant was absent from gnomAD, ExAC, and 1000 Genomes, and it affected a highly conserved residue in the fifth transmembrane helix of domain IV. Structural modeling suggested that the residue faces the pore-forming sixth helix, and the authors concluded that the substitution likely disrupts channel gating. The patient also carried a de novo deletion of MSH2 exons 11-16.
quotes: Trio ES revealed a heterozygous de novo variant in CACNA1C (NM_000719.6: c.4087G>A, p.V1363M). The amino acid position is highly conserved, is absent from control databases such as gnomAD, ExAC, and 1000 Genomes, and has not been previously reported as a pathogenic variant.
V1363M localizes in the fifth TMH in domain IV
A change from valine to methionine, a larger residue, likely disrupts the protein structure in the sixth TMH, affecting the gating or calcium transmission of Cav1.2.

findings.statement: Bozarth et al. (2018) described a family of Irish and German descent. The proband (Patient 2), a girl, had tetralogy of Fallot, which was repaired at 2 months, and developed severe biventricular failure with left ventricular noncompaction at 4 months. She also had mild dysmorphic features, including flat nasal bridge, low-set cupped ears, deep-set eyes, thin upper lip, and round face, along with mild 2-3-4 toe syndactyly, mild developmental delay, and mild hypotonia. Her father (Patient 3) had a congenital ventricular septal defect and aortic valve stenosis, learning disabilities, and ADHD. He developed focal-to-generalized tonic-clonic seizures at age 18 years and had craniofacial features similar to his daughter's.
quotes: ECHO demonstrated TOF which was surgically repaired at 2 months of age. Subsequently, at 4 months of life, she developed acute severe biventricular failure requiring inotropic support and mechanical ventilation. ECHO demonstrated left ventricular noncompaction (LVNC).
At 8 months, she had mild developmental delays. By 12 months, she spoke 10 words and first walked. Her neurologic exam showed mild diffuse hypotonia.

Her father, who also carried the splice site variant in CACNA1C, had a congenital ventricular septal defect and aortic valve stenosis which was repaired at age 2.5 months. In addition, he had learning disabilities requiring individualized education program at school and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). By 18 years, he developed seizures.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with focal onset

findings.statement: In Patient 2, Bozarth et al. (2018) used a 120-gene cardiomyopathy panel to identify a heterozygous splice site variant in the CACNA1C gene: c.3717+1_3717+2insA (NM_000719.6). The variant was inherited from her affected father (Patient 3), was absent from population databases, and was predicted to destroy the canonical splice donor site of intron 28. In the absence of mRNA studies it was classified as a VUS, although the authors proposed that haploinsufficiency could explain the phenotype. The proband also carried a heterozygous ALPK3 splice variant and a TPM1 p.I130T variant; the TPM1 variant was absent in her father.
quotes: The first was a heterozygous CACNA1C splice site variant (NM_000719.6: c.3717+1_3717+2insA) that was paternally inherited. This variant has not been previously reported in the literature, is absent from large control population databases, and is predicted to destroy the canonical splice donor site in intron 28
we propose this splice site variant and haploinsufficiency can also account for the phenotype in Timothy syndrome. Future mRNA studies are needed to bolster this proposal.

findings.statement: Bozarth et al. (2018) noted that seizures had rarely been reported in CACNA1C-related disorders, with only 3 individuals reported before their series. They concluded that their findings extend the phenotype to neonatal-onset epileptic encephalopathy and late-onset epilepsy, and that Family 2 shows variable expressivity. They suggested including CACNA1C on epilepsy gene panels.
quotes: seizures are rarely reported in CACNA1C–related disorders with only 3 previously reported individuals prior to our case series. We expand upon this with an infant presenting with NOEE and an adult with late seizure onset.
With this information, we propose the consideration of including the CACNA1C in early-onset epilepsy gene panels.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with a de novo heterozygous CACNA1C variant who had syndactyly and developmental delay but no QT prolongation. This is a non-cardiac CACNA1C neurodevelopmental phenotype.

findings.statement: Kosaki et al. (2018) reported a 5-year-old girl with cutaneous syndactyly, developmental delay, and pulmonary hypertension. She did not have prolongation of the QT interval. The authors described her condition as Timothy syndrome-like.
quotes: Here, we report a 5-year-old female patient with cutaneous syndactyly, developmental delay, and pulmonary hypertension.
this patient is the first to exhibit syndactyly and to carry a CACNA1C mutation but to not have QT prolongation

findings.statement: In a 5-year-old girl with syndactyly, developmental delay, and pulmonary hypertension but no QT prolongation, Kosaki et al. (2018) used exome analysis to identify a de novo heterozygous variant in the CACNA1C gene, p.Arg1024Gly, which had not been described before.
quotes: Exome analysis showed a previously undescribed de novo heterozygous mutation in the CACNA1C gene, p.Arg1024Gly.
